_doc: THE LIGHTING CENSUS — the five frozen figures tests/lint/sovereigntyLightingContract.walker.test.js
asserts against the live estate. EXTRACTED from that file's inline constant by TE-EFF-1 car 2
(ODQ §778.2) for one measured reason: EVERY landing on the night of 2026-08-29/30 conflicted on
that one line. Two lanes measuring the same instrument from the same base produce tuples that are
each correct and jointly meaningless, so the conflict could never be resolved by hand-arithmetic —
only by re-measuring. Moving the tuple to its own file makes the correct resolution the CHEAP one:
⛔ NEVER HAND-EDIT THE FIVE FIGURES. They are actuals out of execution, and a hand-composed number
here is exactly the 'stale numeral' class the walker exists to refuse. Regenerate instead:
LIGHTING_CENSUS_REFREEZE='<lane or seat id>' LIGHTING_CENSUS_NOTE='<why it moved>' \
That command REFUSES to run on a dirty tree (a shared working tree can hold another lane's
uncommitted test files, and measuring then charges their files to you and writes a number no
checkout can reproduce — ES-1 was bitten by exactly this and had to re-measure on a `git archive`
of its own parent). It writes all five or none, and it EXITS NON-ZERO BY DESIGN so a refreeze can
never be mistaken for a passing gate: re-run the walker plainly afterwards, and that green is the
The derivation history — every prior row, its cause, and the census laws — stays in the walker
beside the assertions, deliberately. Only the live tuple moved.
